title: Courage, My Soul! Behold the Prize
description: Courage, My Soul! Behold the Prize in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 76, “There the weary are at rest”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Cou-rage, my soul! be-hold the prize The Sa-vior's love pro-vides; E-ter-nal life be-yond the skies, For all whom here he guides.

lines: Courage, my soul! behold the prize
The Savior's love provides;
Eternal life beyond the skies,
For all whom here he guides.
The wicked cease from troubling there,
The weary are at rest;
Sorrow and sin, and pain and care,
No more approach the blest.
A wicked world and wicked heart,
With Satan now are joined;
Each acts a too successful part
In harassing my mind.
In conflict with this threefold troop,
How weary, Lord, am I?
Did not thy promise bear me up,
My soul must faint and die.
But fighting in my Savior's strength,
Though mighty are my foes,
I shall a conqu'ror be at length,
O'er all that can oppose.
Then why, my soul, complain or fear?
The crown of glory see!
The more I toil and suffer here,
The sweeter rest will be.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
